reason: H0 never enables WUFFS_XZ__QUIRK_DECODE_STANDALONE_CONCATENATED_STREAMS, so standalone-format decoding remains false and the new concatenated-stream state machine is unreachable. Consequently, fuzzing does not cover multiple XZ Streams, four-byte Stream Padding consumption, continuation after a Stream footer, reset of started_verify_index and per-stream block counters, or the new concatenated-stream error behavior.
evidence: S1 adds QUIRK_DECODE_STANDALONE_CONCATENATED_STREAMS and stores its positive value in decoder.standalone_format via decoder.set_quirk!.
H0's only wuffs_xz__decoder__set_quirk call uses WUFFS_BASE__QUIRK_IGNORE_CHECKSUM; it never uses WUFFS_XZ__QUIRK_DECODE_STANDALONE_CONCATENATED_STREAMS.
In decoder.do_transform_io?, `if not this.standalone_format { break.streams }` bypasses all new Stream Padding and subsequent-Stream logic under H0.

The bypassed branch consumes zero-valued four-byte padding units, recognizes a following `\xFD\x37\x7A\x58` header prefix, returns `#bad header (concatenated stream)` for other words, and resets `this.started_verify_index` before the next Stream.

S1 resets `this.num_actual_blocks` at each Stream header and `this.num_index_blocks` when beginning Index verification, state transitions that matter specifically when one decoder processes multiple Streams.
recommended_action: Extend H0 to derive a fuzz-controlled value from `hash` and call `wuffs_xz__decoder__set_quirk(&dec, WUFFS_XZ__QUIRK_DECODE_STANDALONE_CONCATENATED_STREAMS, value)`, while retaining coverage of the zero/default mode. Seed or structure inputs for multiple valid Streams, zero Stream Padding in multiples of four, truncated padding, nonzero padding/header words, and boundaries delivered through short reads.
